title: TKI 3 · Castle Top
summary: Build the first-bag T-Spin Double of the Castle Top variation. Later bags extend it into more spins.
when: Look for an early I; learn the mirror for the opposite piece order.
steps: Lay I horizontally near the middle, then build the L support at the left wall.
Fit O in the right corner and S beside it. Place Z across the I to shape the roof.
Stand J above O. The diagram shows all seven pieces immediately before the first double clears.
Bring T into the left cavity and finish with a rotation before locking.
tips: Practice checks the first bag, not the entire multi-bag opener.
After the first double, study the remaining surface instead of memorizing only an opening picture.

title: DT Cannon
summary: A T-Spin Double followed by a T-Spin Triple. The initial T helps construct the setup.
when: Choose an LS or JZ base when the opening queue supports it.
steps: Read the first bag and choose the matching base in the source diagrams.
Keep the entry channel open while building the double above the triple cavity.
Use the next T for the double, then rotate a later T into the exposed triple.
Continue into ordinary stacking, another spin pattern, or a perfect-clear branch.
tips: Free practice is a sandbox; it does not validate a complete DT Cannon.
Learn the entry rotations before trying to build this quickly.

title: Perfect Clear Opener
summary: Arrange the first bag to leave a four-row puzzle for the second bag. A perfect clear is a possible finish, not a guarantee.
when: Useful when you want to practice reading small empty regions.
steps: Combine J, O, and L into the rectangular side of the setup.
Build the staggered T, S, and Z shape on the other side.
Keep I available when possible; the displayed variant places it vertically.
Inspect the next pieces and fill the gap without leaving isolated holes.
tips: The diagram is a first-bag reference, not a guaranteed solution.
Switch to normal stacking if the queue or incoming garbage spoils the clear.

title: Grace System
summary: An alternative first perfect-clear setup that can complement PCO when its initial construction fits.
when: Consider it when you can assemble its rectangle while saving T.
steps: Compare your starting queue with the source setup before committing.
Build the six-column, four-row rectangle and preserve the T when possible.
Read the remaining four-column region against the next pieces.
Choose a compatible solve or leave a manageable stack if no solve is available.
tips: Holding T and holding I lead to different perfect-clear problems.
Free practice does not judge whether you reproduced Grace System.

title: MKO Stacking
summary: An early L/J setup with perfect-clear opportunities and T-Spin continuations.
when: Use it when L and J can be placed before their supported S/Z pieces.
steps: Use the diagram to build the first-bag base; keep T in hold.
Check the second bag for a four-line perfect-clear solution.
If the solve is unavailable, make a T-slot and continue with doubles.
Flatten the residue into a sustainable midgame stack.
tips: An early second T can make the continuation awkward.
The shown base intentionally contains six pieces: its T is held.

title: Albatross Special
summary: Learn the first-bag platform T-Spin Double. The wider opener can continue with a triple.
when: An early O makes the platform practical; choose the mirror from the J/L order.
steps: Place O near the left, I against the right wall, and S at the left wall.
Use L to support J; put Z above the O/L side to form the roof.
Rotate T beneath the roof to complete the two filled rows shown in the diagram.
Study the triple continuation separately after mastering this first bag.
tips: This practice checks the first double only.
Garbage can disrupt the later triple.

title: Hachispin
summary: Start with a T-Spin Single, develop a triple, and look for a perfect-clear continuation.
when: A useful early-O alternative when your usual TKI or DT base does not fit.
steps: Choose the source first-bag pattern that matches your queue.
Build and execute its opening single without burying the next entry.
Select the second-bag triple construction from the pieces you receive.
After the triple, attempt a matching perfect clear or return to ordinary stacking.
tips: A perfect-clear branch is optional, not assured.
The setup restricts downstacking until the triple is executed.

title: Single Double PC
summary: A single-to-double opener with optional extra-spin and perfect-clear continuations.
when: Consider it with an early O and time to perform the required soft drops.
steps: Build the opening horizontal T-Spin Single shown in the source.
Preserve the remaining structure for the second-bag double.
Read the third bag for a compatible perfect-clear solve.
Keep the field clean enough to continue stacking when the solve does not fit.
tips: This is related to Stickspin, but the opening T is used differently.
Free practice is ungraded and does not confirm the whole sequence.

title: Stickspin · First Single
summary: Build Stickspin’s first-bag vertical T-Spin Single. Later bags develop a double and a triple.
when: The O needs to support the right-hand structure before the relevant S or T.
steps: Stand I against the left wall. Fit L and J beside it.
Place O in the right corner, then Z along the floor beside O.
Stand S above O and rotate T into the vertical slot.
Lock T to clear the first single. The diagram shows this moment before the clear.
tips: Success here means the first bag is complete, not the entire Stickspin.
Learn the second-bag double before attempting the full three-bag sequence.

title: BT Cannon
summary: An offset double-to-triple construction with longer C-Spin and perfect-clear branches.
when: Study it after you can recognize ordinary DT Cannon cavities.
steps: Identify the double slot and the offset hole underneath it in the source diagram.
Build the first bags without sealing the T entry.
Execute the double, then the triple revealed below it.
Choose the correct C-Spin branch only if the later queue and field allow it.
tips: Learn one branch at a time rather than memorizing a five-bag picture.
Its shape is related to DT Cannon, but the placements are not interchangeable.

title: C-Spin
summary: A triple-to-double attack built around a C-shaped J/L overhang.
when: The common ZST-core opener is worth studying when S and Z arrive early.
steps: Use S, Z, and T to form the low central core in the reference diagram.
Build the J/L overhang without blocking the triple entry.
Stack the second bag to complete the triple and its exit.
Execute the triple, then use the remaining cavity for a double.
tips: The diagram is the first-bag base, not the finished attack.
The second bag often requires adaptation rather than one fixed sequence.

title: Pelican
summary: A platform-double alternative for awkward S/Z/T starts, with related triple continuations.
when: Compare J and L arrival order before choosing which side to build.
steps: Choose the side from the early J/L order.
Prop S for the left-facing version, or Z for the mirror.
Keep the platform entry open and finish the double with T.
Use the source continuation only when its required second-bag pieces fit.
tips: This is related to Albatross but uses a different base.
Do not force the triple after the structure has been disrupted.

title: Side 4-Wide
summary: Leave a four-column combo well beside a six-column stack.
when: Practice consecutive single clears rather than one large attack.
steps: Keep four columns open along an edge while stacking the other six.
Preserve a small residue inside the well.
Place each successive piece to clear a line and continue the combo.
Stop building upward when you need to defend or downstack.
tips: A tall side stack can be topped out before its combo is ready.
A misplaced piece that clears nothing ends the combo.

title: Center 4-Wide
summary: Build two side towers around a four-column central combo well.
when: Study it after learning the piece sequences of a side 4-wide.
steps: Reserve the central four columns for the combo.
Build three-column towers on both sides while keeping their surfaces manageable.
Preserve the well’s residue and clear with consecutive pieces.
Watch both tower heights and abandon the setup when defense requires it.
tips: The well uses the same combo ideas as side 4-wide.
Keeping two narrow towers balanced is harder than building one broad stack.

title: T-Spin · Recognition
summary: A T-spin can count even when it clears no line.
when: Learn recognition before larger clears.
steps: Find the T’s center and its four diagonal corners.
Fill three corners. Make your last successful movement a rotation.
Lock without shifting or falling afterward.
tips: Walls and the floor count as occupied space.
A full spin and a mini have different front-corner requirements.

title: T-Spin Single
summary: Rotate T into a three-corner cavity that completes one row.
when: Use a single when the surrounding stack cannot support a double.
steps: Bring T to the slot’s entrance.
Rotate into the cavity and check the corners.
Lock after the rotation while completing exactly one row.
tips: A single is about rows cleared, not the T’s orientation.
A final downward movement can remove spin recognition.

title: T-Spin Double
summary: Fill a T-shaped cavity to clear two rows with a recognized rotation.
when: A compact way to attack while keeping the stack low.
steps: Approach the cavity without sealing its entrance.
Soft drop to its mouth, then rotate under the overhang.
Lock after the final rotation completes two rows.
tips: The two rows must already be nearly complete.
Practice the mirrored slot as well.

title: T-Spin Mini
summary: Recognize a three-corner T placement with only one occupied front corner.
when: Useful for understanding why a move scores as a mini rather than a full spin.
steps: Identify the two corners on the side the T points toward.
Rotate into a position with three occupied corners overall.
Lock and compare the front corners with a full T-spin cavity.
tips: The special final SRS kick can upgrade some placements to full spins.
A mini is a scoring classification, not simply a small-looking rotation.

title: T-Spin Triple
summary: Use an SRS kick to rotate T into a tall cavity and complete three rows.
when: Study this before attempting the second attack of a DT Cannon.
steps: Check that three rows can be completed by a vertical T.
Approach beneath the overhang using the orientation shown by the source.
Rotate to trigger the kick into the deep cavity, then lock after the final rotation.
Trace the entry first; this reference lesson has no preset triple challenge.
tips: A tall T-shaped hole alone does not guarantee a reachable triple.
The wall opposite the overhang can affect whether the entry works.

title: I-Piece Wall Kick
summary: Rotate I beside a wall and let its dedicated kick table shift it into a legal position.
when: Useful when a long piece seems unable to turn near the edge.
steps: Move I toward the wall in the starting orientation.
Try the requested quarter-turn and observe the sideways adjustment.
Place it in the target footprint after the kick.
tips: I uses different kick offsets from J, L, S, T, and Z.
Clockwise and counterclockwise routes need not produce the same result.

title: T-Piece Floor Kick
summary: Rotate a grounded T when the normal rotation collides with the floor.
when: Learn how kicks can lift a piece before returning to a landing position.
steps: Bring T to the floor in the exercise’s starting orientation.
Rotate through the blocked orientation so SRS searches its kick offsets.
Observe the lift or shift, then finish in the target cells.
tips: A floor kick is not automatically a scored T-spin.
Three occupied corners and the final rotation still matter for spin scoring.

title: J and L Tucks
summary: Rotate a hook beneath an overhang instead of dropping it straight down.
when: Useful for repairing a small cavity or solving a perfect-clear region.
steps: Turn J toward the opening and lower it beside the overhang.
Rotate back into the horizontal cavity; L uses the mirrored route.
Finish in the target footprint before locking.
tips: These are movement techniques; bostris awards special spin scoring only to T.
A J route cannot be copied to L without mirroring the rotations and geometry.

title: T-Spin Double · Mirrored
summary: Fill a T-shaped cavity to clear two rows with a recognized rotation.
when: Use the same slot recognition when the overhang faces the other way.
steps: Identify the two nearly complete rows and the mirrored T-shaped cavity.
The T starts vertically at the entrance, with its arm pointing left.
Rotate counterclockwise once to fit the outline.
Hard drop immediately without shifting or lowering the T after rotating.
tips: Clockwise and counterclockwise are not interchangeable inside a tight slot.
Look at the front corners of the final T to recognize a full spin.

title: L-Piece Tuck
summary: Rotate an L under an overhang. This is a placement technique; the game awards spin scoring only to T pieces.
when: Useful when a block overhang prevents a straight drop into an L-shaped space.
steps: Notice the roof above the outlined placement.
The L starts vertically beside the opening.
Rotate counterclockwise once to tuck its arm under the roof.
Hard drop to lock in the outline.
tips: This is the mirror of the J tuck.
A successful tuck does not earn a T-spin scoring bonus.
